derivation.validated_on: 2026 week 7 re-simulated from the archived fixture

notes: Applied AFTER every promoted synthesis sets the mean, so the QB M89/M90 and RB P3 mean invariants (AGENTS.md section 7) are untouched; validation measured the worst relative mean shift at 0.00000.
Widen-then-clip was REJECTED: it lifts a low-mean players mean by up to 27.8% because clipping at zero is not mean-preserving.
A market absent from this file is left UNCHANGED (k=1.0) and labelled, rather than failing the slate.

This is a calibration of dispersion, not a structural fix. The underlying cause is that simulation_v2 draws outcome noise conditional on point-estimate ypt/ypc/catch_rate/share with no sampling of their own uncertainty. That remains open.
promotion_blocker: GPT audit 6472971619 section 3: the week-7 validation recalibrated RAW simulation_v2 draws, not the distribution production actually prices. Production inserts this transform after the V3/V6/V5/V1 wrapper chain, QB attempt conversion, ensemble mean construction, M89/M90 synthesis and the target_mean/mc_proj mean alignment, and before align_prealigned_outcomes. The reported Brier 0.2713->0.2555 is therefore a raw-simulator counterfactual. k is NOT promoted and is inert in live pricing until an exact production-path baseline-parity replay certifies it.
purpose: Mean-preserving dispersion scale for the empirical Monte Carlo pricing distribution. Production prices from np.mean(adjusted_outcomes > line); those draws were measurably under-dispersed, making probabilities overconfident. k widens the draws about their own mean without moving it.
